fields.name: Groups
fields.evidence: Constructor bg3.exe+0x1C6FD20; destructor bg3.exe+0x6CDBB0 -> bg3.exe+0x6D3660 walks values with stride 0x40 and frees an array at value + 0x30 (each value is itself a 64-byte hash map). Keys are 16 bytes: bg3.exe+0x2042EB0 walks the key array at +0x20 with stride 0x10 and passes each key to the Guid-keyed lookups of ecl::TimelineMaterialComponent (bg3.exe+0x1D746D0) and of ecl::TimelineSystem+0x430 (material groups). The macOS build names the type ls::HashMap<ls::Guid, ls::HashMap<ls::FixedString, ecl::EmotionMaterialParam>> (destructor instantiation bg3_macos_x64 0x100E67DD8; SetParam looks up the Guid, then Ensure<FixedString> on the inner map). Inner value size on Windows not established (see TimelineEmotionMaterialParam).

fields.name: Targets
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2043070 looks up MaterialTargetDetails::GroupId (element + 8 of MaterialConfiguration::MaterialDetails) in comp + 0x40 and reads values with stride 0x48; destructor bg3.exe+0x6D14C0 confirms the stride.

fields.name: field_80
fields.evidence: Destructor bg3.exe+0x6CDBB0 -> bg3.exe+0x6DF1F0: element stride 0x20; cleared by bg3.exe+0x2042EB0 when the emotion track stops. Probably ls::DynamicArray<ecl::TimelineEmotionMaterialComponent::GroupCache> (macOS destructor instantiation next to the component's ops); macOS SetParam appends 0x20-byte elements to the array at +0x80.
